description: Recovery: give an overturned car a route back (brief Task 3). Confirmed by reading the code: VehicleJumpFlip.CanFlipNow and TryFlip both require _controller.IsGrounded, flipRequiresGrounded is 1 on all three profiles, and IsGrounded comes from suspension rays cast along -transform.up, which point at the sky when the car is on its roof - so the player's own recovery input is refused in exactly the state it exists for. CORRECTION to the brief's premise, found during planning: VehicleController DOES already have an automatic path the earlier investigation missed. FixedUpdate step 8 calls ApplyStuckRecovery, which applies rightingTorque (8 rad/s^2) about Cross(transform.up, Vector3.up) once Uprightness < 0.35 and Speed < 1.2 have held for 1.5 s, and all three profiles ship it on. Three real gaps remain: the flip key still does nothing; the 0.35 gate misses a car wedged on its side between 0.35 and 0.5 uprightness (0.5 is the project's own IsUpright line) where no wheel is down either; and whether 8 rad/s^2 actually rolls a 900 kg box off its roof cannot be known without Unity. This feature adds a deterministic, player-triggered self-right on the EXISTING Flip action plus a 3 s no-input backstop, and does not touch a single tuning value. Independent of FEAT-001; FEAT-003 depends on the SelfRightCount counter added here.

Read-only, applies no force. Document why world down.

In the same file extract `public void SetPoseAndClearMotion(Vector3 position, Quaternion rotation)` from the first half of Teleport: the interpolation off/on trick that clears the position history, the _rb.position / _rb.rotation / transform.SetPositionAndRotation write, zeroing linearVelocity and angularVelocity, and _stuckTimer = 0f so the auto-right timer and this recovery do not fight. Then make Teleport call it and keep only its measurement-specific tail (Drive = default, SteerAmount = 0f, _steerVelocity = 0f, and the boost resets). Behaviour for the measurement harness must be byte-identical. Say in the XML doc that recovery deliberately uses the pose half only, because refilling BoostRemaining would make rolling the car the cheapest way to buy boost and would corrupt boost_earned in the shift log. Change NO line of ApplyDriveAndBrake, ApplySteering, ApplyLateralGrip, ApplyLateralGripPerAxle, ApplyAxleGrip, ApplySuspension, ApplyBoost, EarnBoost or ApplyStuckRecovery.

In Assets/Project/Scripts/Vehicle/VehicleJumpFlip.cs add a [Header("Self right")] block of [Tooltip]+[SerializeField] fields at the defaults in plan.md item 7: selfRightEnabled true, selfRightUprightThreshold 0.5, selfRightHoldTime 0.6, selfRightMaxSpeed 2, selfRightMaxAngularSpeed 1.5, selfRightGroundProbe 2, selfRightRideHeight 0.8, selfRightCooldown 2, selfRightAutoAfterSeconds 3. Use the tooltip wording from the plan; it names each precedent (0.5 = VehicleController.IsUpright, 2 < driftMinimumSpeed 4, 0.8 = the spawn height every scene uses, 3 = twice the tuning asset's 1.5 s righting-torque delay).

Add the readable surface in the file's existing style: `public int SelfRightCount { get; private set; }`, `public float SelfRightCooldownRemaining { get; private set; }`, `public bool CanSelfRightNow { get; private set; }`, and optionally `public event Action SelfRighted;` mirroring FlipStarted.

Write UpdateOverturnedState(float dt), called from FixedUpdate before the queued-input dispatch. Accumulate _overturnedFor only while ALL of: Uprightness < selfRightUprightThreshold, Speed < selfRightMaxSpeed, _rb.angularVelocity.magnitude < selfRightMaxAngularSpeed, !_controller.IsDrifting, and _controller.ProbeGroundBelow(selfRightGroundProbe, out _groundHit) returns true. Otherwise reset it to 0. Tick SelfRightCooldownRemaining down with the other cooldowns and set CanSelfRightNow = selfRightEnabled && _overturnedFor >= selfRightHoldTime && SelfRightCooldownRemaining <= 0f && !IsFlipping.

Write TrySelfRight() per plan.md item 7: flatten transform.forward onto the world XZ plane with the same two fallbacks ReadGround uses (transform.up projected, then Vector3.forward), build Quaternion.LookRotation(flat, Vector3.up), place the car at _groundHit.point + Vector3.up * selfRightRideHeight, call _controller.SetPoseAndClearMotion, reset _overturnedFor, set SelfRightCooldownRemaining = selfRightCooldown, increment SelfRightCount, raise the event, return true. Add a Refuse(reason) line for each gate so the existing logRefusals toggle explains a refusal the way it does for jump and flip.

Change the FixedUpdate dispatch so a queued flip is spent on recovery when the car is overturned and resting: `if (_flipQueued && CanSelfRightNow && TrySelfRight()) _flipQueued = false; else if (_flipQueued && TryFlip()) _flipQueued = false;` then the no-input backstop `if (selfRightAutoAfterSeconds > 0f && _overturnedFor >= selfRightAutoAfterSeconds && CanSelfRightNow) TrySelfRight();`. Do not add a new input action: the README Controls table is contract-tested against VehicleControls.inputactions by docs/tooling/repo-checks/test_documents.py, and reusing Flip is also what a tester already tries.

Confirm the lab is undisturbed: read VehicleMeasurement.cs:553 and :645 and check that the car is reset upright and settled there, so Uprightness is about 1 and CanSelfRightNow is false, leaving the F4 flip measurement reaching TryFlip exactly as before. Record the conclusion in findings.

Extend the class XML doc's 'WHAT THIS IS NOT FOR' rules with the self-right: it redirects nothing, grants no speed, zeroes velocity, is gated on a sustained resting overturned state, and has its own cooldown, so it cannot be a corner shortcut or an air dash.

Run the verification commands. Change no value in Tuning_Balanced.asset, Tuning_Grippy.asset or Tuning_Loose.asset: if the only way to make the car recover appears to be raising rightingTorque, STOP and report it instead.
Commit locally on fix/reverse-and-recovery with a subject <= 72 chars and a why-body; check `git diff --cached --name-only` first.

WHAT WAS IMPLEMENTED. VehicleController gained two additive members and one behaviour-preserving extraction, and no line of ApplyDriveAndBrake, ApplySteering, ApplyLateralGrip, ApplyLateralGripPerAxle, ApplyAxleGrip, ApplySuspension, ApplyBoost, EarnBoost or ApplyStuckRecovery was touched. (1) `public bool ProbeGroundBelow(float distance, out RaycastHit hit)` placed next to TryRaycast: one TryRaycast from transform.position along WORLD Vector3.down, so it reuses the existing own-collider filter and tuning.groundMask, returns false when tuning is null, applies no force and writes no state. World down is the point: the suspension rays run along -transform.up, which on an inverted car aims at the sky. (2) `public void SetPoseAndClearMotion(Vector3 position, Quaternion rotation)` holds the first half of the old Teleport verbatim: the _rb == null fallback, the interpolation off/on trick that clears the position history, the _rb.position / _rb.rotation / transform.SetPositionAndRotation write, zeroing linearVelocity and angularVelocity, and _stuckTimer = 0f. (3) Teleport is now SetPoseAndClearMotion(position, rotation) followed by only the measurement-specific tail: Drive = default, SteerAmount = 0f, _steerVelocity = 0f and the unchanged boost block (BoostRemaining = tuning.boostCapacity, _boostRechargeCountdown, IsBoosting, IsSupersonic, IsEarningBoost, BoostEarnedThisStep, TotalBoostEarned). The harness sees identical behaviour: the same statements run in the same effective order, with _stuckTimer = 0f simply moved earlier inside the same call, which cannot be observed because nothing between the two points reads it.

VehicleJumpFlip gained a [Header("Self right")] block of nine [Tooltip] + [SerializeField] private fields at the plan's defaults (selfRightEnabled true, selfRightUprightThreshold 0.5, selfRightHoldTime 0.6, selfRightMaxSpeed 2, selfRightMaxAngularSpeed 1.5, selfRightGroundProbe 2, selfRightRideHeight 0.8, selfRightCooldown 2, selfRightAutoAfterSeconds 3), with the plan's tooltip wording naming each precedent. They sit on the MonoBehaviour, not on VehicleTuning, because the three profiles are frozen for this task; a scene saved before the fields existed carries no entry for them, so Unity falls back to the C# initialisers and NO SCENE EDIT IS NEEDED. Private state: `_overturnedFor` and `_groundHit`. UpdateOverturnedState(dt) runs from FixedUpdate right after AgeQueuedInput and before the dispatch; it ticks SelfRightCooldownRemaining down, accumulates _overturnedFor only while Uprightness < 0.5 AND Speed < 2 AND _rb.angularVelocity.magnitude < 1.5 AND !IsDrifting AND ProbeGroundBelow(2, out _groundHit) all hold, resets it to 0 otherwise, and sets CanSelfRightNow = selfRightEnabled && _overturnedFor >= selfRightHoldTime && SelfRightCooldownRemaining <= 0f && !IsFlipping. TrySelfRight() re-checks every gate with its own Refuse(reason) line so logRefusals explains a refusal the way it does for jump and flip, then flattens transform.forward onto world XZ with the two fallbacks ReadGround uses (transform.up projected, then Vector3.forward), builds Quaternion.LookRotation(flat.normalized, Vector3.up), places the car at _groundHit.point + Vector3.up * selfRightRideHeight, calls _controller.SetPoseAndClearMotion, resets _overturnedFor, sets the cooldown, increments SelfRightCount, clears CanSelfRightNow and raises SelfRighted. The dispatch is now `if (_flipQueued && CanSelfRightNow && TrySelfRight()) _flipQueued = false; else if (_flipQueued && TryFlip()) _flipQueued = false;` followed by the backstop `if (selfRightAutoAfterSeconds > 0f && _overturnedFor >= selfRightAutoAfterSeconds && CanSelfRightNow) TrySelfRight();`. NO NEW INPUT ACTION: the Flip binding (Q) carries the second meaning, so VehicleControls.inputactions and the README Controls table are both untouched and test_readme_controls_have_required_actions_and_bindings still passes. The class XML doc gained rule 4 under WHAT THIS IS NOT FOR: the self-right redirects nothing, grants no speed (velocity and spin are zeroed, so it always costs the player everything they had), is gated on a sustained resting overturned state, and has its own cooldown.

RECOVERY NEVER CALLS TELEPORT, so BoostRemaining and TotalBoostEarned are untouched by a self-right and boost_earned in the shift log keeps describing driving. That is stated in the XML doc on both SetPoseAndClearMotion and at the call site in TrySelfRight.

THE CORRECTION ABOUT ApplyStuckRecovery STANDS AND NOTHING WAS DONE TO IT. VehicleController.FixedUpdate step 8 still calls ApplyStuckRecovery(dt), which still applies tuning.rightingTorque about Cross(transform.up, Vector3.up) once Uprightness < stuckUprightThreshold and Speed < stuckSpeedThreshold have held for stuckTimeBeforeRighting. Not one line of it changed and not one tuning value changed: rightingTorque is still 8, stuckUprightThreshold 0.35, stuckSpeedThreshold 1.2, stuckTimeBeforeRighting 1.5, autoRightWhenStuck on, on all three profiles. The two paths are deliberately layered rather than competing: the torque gets 1.5 s to work, a flip press can take over from 0.6 s, and the no-input backstop fires at 3 s, which is twice the torque's own delay. SetPoseAndClearMotion zeroes _stuckTimer so the torque's countdown restarts after a recovery instead of carrying in seconds already spent on the roof.

THE F4 FLIP MEASUREMENT PATH IS UNAFFECTED, confirmed by reading the two call sites. MeasureFlipDistance (VehicleMeasurement.cs around :603-:645) calls ResetCar(StartPose()), waits Settle(0.4f), drives to flipTestSpeed, then spins on `while (!jumpFlip.CanFlipNow ...)` before RequestFlip(flipTestDirection). The car is upright and moving there, so Uprightness is about 1, which is above selfRightUprightThreshold 0.5, so the overturned gate is false, _overturnedFor stays 0 and CanSelfRightNow is false. The dispatch's first branch short-circuits on CanSelfRightNow before TrySelfRight is ever entered, so the queued flip reaches TryFlip exactly as before and FlipCount still increments, which is the condition the harness waits on. The wall-recovery test (:553) is the same story from the other direction: it requests a backwards flip while holding full reverse throttle, so Speed is above selfRightMaxSpeed 2 for most of the window and the car is upright anyway; even in the worst case the 0.6 s hold would have to be satisfied first, and the self-right would be the correct outcome of a car that had actually ended up on its roof against the wall. No lab behaviour changed and no measurement is invalidated.

NOT SETTLEABLE WITHOUT A UNITY PLAY TEST. All nine knobs are serialized, so every number below can be retuned in the inspector without a recompile. Open Assets/Project/Scenes/Possible game scene.unity in Unity 6000.5.4f1 with logRefusals on and:
  1. CAN THE CAR REST INVERTED AT ALL? The body collider is a long flat 1.8 x 1.0 x 4.2 m box, which tends to fall back onto its wheels, and `flips` is 0 in all 7 logged rows, so no human has ever been observed in this state. Flip the car onto its roof against a kerb or a wall on purpose and see whether it stays there. If it cannot be made to stay, the self-right is insurance rather than a fix and should be left at its defaults.
  2. DOES rightingTorque 8 ROLL IT OVER FIRST? Get it inverted and press nothing. The automatic torque has 1.5 s before it is even applied and the backstop fires at 3 s. If the torque rights the car inside that window, the backstop never fires in practice. If the torque cannot right it, DO NOT RAISE rightingTorque: the number lives in all three frozen Tuning_*.asset files, and the new self-right is the deterministic route back precisely so the torque does not have to be touched. Report it instead.
  3. IS 0.8 m OF RIDE HEIGHT ENOUGH? 0.8 is the spawn height every scene uses with the floor plate at y = 0, but in Hard/Medium the city sits roughly 0.4 m above that plate. Self-right on a raised road, on a kerb, under an overpass and on a ramp, and confirm the car does not spawn intersecting geometry or drop noticeably. The probe takes _groundHit.point, so it should follow the raised surface; what is unverified is clearance ABOVE the car in a tunnel or under a bridge, which nothing in the gate checks.
  4. THE KEY ITSELF. On the roof, press Q and confirm the car rights after about 0.6 s facing the way it was facing. Repeat and press nothing: confirm it rights itself within about 3 s.
  5. NO FALSE POSITIVES. Drive normally for 60 s, jumping, flipping and drifting hard, and confirm SelfRightCount stays 0 and no self-right line appears in the console. Drifting needs Speed at or above driftMinimumSpeed 4 and the gate caps speed at 2, so a drift should be unreachable by construction; the case worth watching is a heavy landing that briefly reads slow, overturned and near ground, which the 0.6 s hold should absorb.
  6. BOOST IS NOT REFUNDED. Spend the tank, self-right, and confirm BoostRemaining does not jump back to capacity (BoostGauge shows it) and that boost_earned in the next logged row is not inflated.
  7. F4 IN VehicleLab after all of the above, to confirm the flip measurement still produces its usual PASS/FAIL and the self-right did not swallow the harness's flip.
